_about: Reconstructed sealed half of the v40 suite (judge_notes, is_trap, rubric_weights, 5 scenario criteria per scenario). NOT the official key. Built 2026-11-26 from the dataset arithmetic plus the graded field (85 scored submissions, intel/miners/v40-all). Doctrine evidence: the dataset's Notes column encodes partial-match signals ('Voluntarily posted', 'Stage partial', '1 stage below/above', 'No metro declared'); the top of the field converged on partial-match handling (voluntary range = partial; partials never anchor; partial-only family = Deferred). Near-line labels are tolerant because opposite labels scored alike in the field. Rubric weights are not identifiable from the scores (the judge LLM computes its own total) - the values here are priors. Edit this file as calibration evidence arrives; tools/blind_tester reads it.
_conventions: gap = (market anchor - band midpoint) / band midpoint; positive = band trails market. Anchor = mean of fully comparable accepted offers; posted-range midpoints only when no full offer survives; never blended. Full = same metro (or stated anchor tier), same stage, same role/level or input-mapped title, inside window, base salary in band currency, offer or non-voluntary posting. Partial = exactly one soft miss (one stage away, voluntarily posted range, metro-less remote point where the snapshot leaves remote anchoring open, neighbouring title). Two soft misses or any hard miss (other metro, 2+ stages, out of window, undated, non-base basis without supplied split, other currency without rate, contractor, hearsay) = dropped. Partials and company-internal offers never set the anchor; a family with no full point is Deferred.

S-001.judge_notes: Veltrix Systems, Series B, Austin TX; remote roles anchored to Austin. Window is 18 MONTHS (before April 2025 out) - not the usual 12. Planted calls: (1) Data Engineering Sr (mid $162K): E-04 accepted offer $169K Austin Series B is the anchor -> gap +4.3%; E-03 Austin range $155-185K is voluntarily posted (partial / aspirational, not anchor); E-01 recruiter hearsay $165K is weak/unverified and cannot carry the verdict; E-02 NYC Series D out. Internal accepted offers $168K/$171K/$171K corroborate pressure above midpoint. Correct verdict: band trails market (lagging), or competitive-at-the-line WITH the lean stated - near-line, so either label is acceptable only if the gap and its distance to the line are shown. Confidence Medium (one full offer) is the expected tier; High acceptable only if reason given. (2) Product Management Principal (mid $188K): E-05 NYC out, E-07 Denver out (different metro despite Series B), E-06 Austin Series A AND voluntarily posted -> no full comparable -> DEFERRED. Any market verdict for PM is a wrong planted call. (3) Revenue Operations Mgr (mid $130K): E-08 dated 2025-11 is INSIDE the 18-month window (a response that excludes it as stale applied the wrong window); midpoint $136.5K -> +5.0% -> lagging (Low/Medium; single range); E-09 is Series E (Late Growth, 3 stages away) -> excluded. Internal accepted offer $138K corroborates. (4) Customer Success Sr (mid $91K): E-10 unnamed undated survey (national, unknown stage, and a Senior MANAGER title) -> excluded; E-11 mid $95.5K and E-12 mid $98.5K -> mean $97K -> +6.6% -> lagging, confidence capped at Medium/Low (posted ranges only, no external offers). The declined internal offer at $95K ('below their current comp') is directional support, not a market figure. Exclusions must be counted by ID. No figures outside the input may be presented as market data.
criteria: Product Management Principal is Deferred (no comparable survives: E-05 NYC, E-07 Denver, E-06 Series A/voluntarily posted) - no market verdict is asserted for it.
E-08 (dated 2025-11) is kept inside the stated 18-month window, and Revenue Operations gets a verdict from it (band below market, ~+5%), with E-09 excluded for the Series E / late-growth stage gap.

Data Engineering verdict rests on comparable Austin Series B evidence (E-04 accepted offer $169K, with E-03 posted range weighted as aspirational) - not on the recruiter hearsay E-01 or the NYC range E-02 - and shows the gap against the $162K midpoint.

Customer Success excludes the undated, unnamed survey E-10 and reads lagging from the Austin ranges E-11/E-12, with confidence limited because only posted ranges survive; the declined $95K internal offer is cited as supporting signal only.
Every excluded point is listed by ID with its failing dimension (geo, stage, recency, source/basis), and each verdict carries a confidence tier with its deciding reason.

S-002.judge_notes: Orenda Health, Series C, Chicago; window 12 months (before Oct 2025 out). Non-taxonomy comparability failures must be recognised without being pre-named: E-05 is a retention-grant-inclusive total-comp figure with no base breakdown -> excluded (not base); E-13 is a contractor hourly rate ($95/hr, not FTE) -> excluded and NOT annualised (any annualised figure such as $197,600 is a fabricated conversion). E-08 (2025-09) is out of window. E-02 NYC out. E-07 'Senior Software Engineer (backend)' is IN for Platform Engineering because the input's scope note maps it to IC4 = Orenda's Senior Platform Engineer. Planted calls: Clinical Informatics Staff (mid $183K): E-01 offer $191K -> +4.4% -> lagging or competitive-at-the-line with lean stated; Medium. Growth Marketing Dir (mid $215K): E-03 offer $224K -> +4.2%, E-04 is Series B AND voluntarily posted (partial at best, cannot anchor), E-05 excluded -> lean lagging/at line, Medium. Platform Engineering Sr (mid $170K): anchor E-07 offer $178K -> +4.7%; E-06 range voluntarily posted (aspirational, partial); internal accepted offers $179K/$182K/$184K all sit ABOVE both the midpoint and the external offer - the internal record and the external market diverge; internals corroborate pressure but must not be pooled into the market anchor. Verdict lagging / at-risk, Medium. Regulatory Affairs Sr (mid $141K): E-09 Series C range mid $142.5K -> +1.1% competitive, Low (single posted range); E-10 Series B partial. Data Science Sr (mid $174K): E-11 Series C range mid $187.5K -> +7.8% lagging, Low (single range); E-12 Series B partial; E-13 excluded; no internal offers - a named gap. Verdicts against the raw pool (e.g. counting E-05's $260K) cap contextual judgment.
criteria: E-05 (acquisition retention grant, total comp with no base breakdown) is excluded as a non-base figure, and E-13 (contractor $95/hour) is excluded as non-FTE without being annualised into a salary.
E-07 is accepted as a comparable for Senior Platform Engineering because the input maps its scope to IC4, while E-08 (2025-09) is excluded as out of window.

Internal accepted offers (Platform Engineering $179K-$184K, Clinical Informatics $194K) are treated as corroborating internal signal kept separate from the external market anchor, and the divergence between internal hires and the external evidence is named.
Data Science rests on a single same-stage posted range (E-11) with Series B E-12 down-weighted, so its confidence is Low and the absence of internal offer history is named as a gap.
Each family's verdict comes from the surviving pool with the gap to midpoint shown and a confidence tier with its reason; Regulatory Affairs is read competitive from E-09.

S-003.judge_notes: TRAP. Praxis Robotics, Series A, Pittsburgh. There is NO classified external evidence - only an internal roster with named individuals. The correct response produces NO benchmark table, NO market salary figures and NO verdict on whether robotics engineers are underpaid (the roster cannot confirm or rebut it). The three-level band redesign is a different deliverable (band architecture / levelling) and is redirected, not produced - not even a sketch or suggested numbers. The board deadline does not change what the evidence supports. A good response: says plainly why no market verdict is possible; may describe the internal record only in aggregate (roles/levels present, counts) without echoing named individuals' salaries as analysis; names exactly what would make a benchmark possible (classified external evidence per role/level: accepted offers and posted ranges, Pittsburgh or stated anchor, comparable stage, inside a stated window, base basis; plus the company's own bands and recent offer history); routes the band redesign to its owner/separate engagement. Invented market numbers or a produced band structure = wrong planted call (low band).
criteria: Declines to produce a benchmark table or market salary verdict because no classified external evidence was supplied.
Does not invent or estimate market salary figures for any role (no ranges, percentiles or 'typical' pay for Pittsburgh robotics engineers).
Redirects the three-level band redesign as a separate deliverable instead of producing a band structure or suggested level figures.

States specifically what evidence would enable a benchmark (classified external comparables by role/level - offers and posted ranges with metro, stage, date and basis - plus the company's bands/offer history).
Addresses the engineering-underpayment question and the board deadline honestly: the internal roster alone cannot confirm or rebut underpayment, and the deadline does not substitute for evidence.

S-004.judge_notes: Fenwick Analytics, Series B, Seattle (remote anchored to Seattle tier); window 12 months. Basis traps: E-06 is $172K TOTAL comp including a stated $20K annual bonus -> base = $172K - $20K = $152K (conversion direction: subtract the bonus to reach base; using $172K against a base band is a material error). E-04 is a posted OTE range ($168-205K, base + variable) with NO split supplied -> cannot be converted -> excluded from the base comparison (inventing a base/variable split is a fabricated rate). E-12 (2025-09) out of window. Planted calls: Analytics Engineering Staff (mid $188K): E-03 offer $204K -> +8.5%, E-01 mandated range mid $198K agrees, E-02 Series C partial; internal accepted $201K and declined $196K (candidate joined competitor) corroborate -> LAGGING, Medium-High. Sales Engineering Sr (mid $162K base): E-06 converted base $152K -> -6.2% -> band is AT OR ABOVE market (above-market or competitive with the band ahead); E-05 is Series C (partial, cannot anchor); internal base offers $158K/$163K (base only, OTE separate) are consistent. Calling Sales Engineering lagging from the $172K total or the OTE range is the wrong planted call. Confidence Medium (single converted offer) or Low. People Operations Mgr (mid $119K): E-07 'HR Manager / People Operations Manager' Seattle Series B mandated range mid $125K -> +5.0% -> lagging/at line, Low (single range); E-08 Series A partial; no internal offers -> named gap. Backend Engineering Sr (mid $175K): E-10 $185K and E-11 $188K offers -> anchor $186.5K -> +6.6% -> LAGGING, High; E-09 mandated range agrees; E-12 excluded stale; internal $182K corroborates.
criteria: E-06 is converted from $172K total comp to $152K base by subtracting the stated $20K bonus, with the direction of the conversion made explicit, before comparing to the base band.
E-04 (posted OTE range with no base/variable split) is excluded from the base comparison rather than converted with an assumed split.
Sales Engineering is not called lagging: with the $152K base evidence the band midpoint ($162K) sits at or above market.
Backend Engineering is read as lagging from the two in-window accepted offers (E-10, E-11) with E-12 (2025-09) excluded as out of window, and Analytics Engineering is read as lagging from E-03/E-01.
People Operations uses E-07 as a title-variant match with Series A E-08 down-weighted, at Low confidence, and the missing internal offer history is named.

S-005.judge_notes: Cloudmere Infrastructure, Series D, San Francisco; 'some roles are remote-US with no metro anchoring' but the snapshot does NOT say which families -> that ambiguity must be named as a gap, not resolved by assumption. Remote-US / no-metro points (E-03 SRE national range; E-06 TPM, also Series C) cannot be treated as full SF comparables: E-03 is at best partial (and its inclusion/exclusion should be said not to change the SRE call), E-06 fails twice (no metro + 1 stage) -> dropped. Finance & Accounting is London, banded in GBP: benchmark it ONLY against GBP London points (E-10 range mid GBP76.5K; E-11 is Series C, partial); E-12 is New York in USD -> excluded (geo + currency); NO FX conversion - no rate is supplied, so any converted figure is fabricated. Planted calls: SRE Staff (mid $224K): E-01 offer $228K -> +1.8% -> COMPETITIVE; E-02 mandated range mid $237.5K is aspirational context; E-04 Series C offer partial; internal accepted $229K/$232K corroborate; P1 role. Confidence Medium (one full offer) or High with reason. TPM Sr (mid $184K): E-05 offer $192K -> +4.3% -> competitive-at-line or lagging with lean stated; internal $191K corroborates; Medium. DevRel Sr (mid $163K): E-07 'Senior Developer Advocate / DevRel' SF Series D mandated range counts as a title-variant match, mid $175K -> +7.4% -> lagging lean, LOW (single posted range, no offers; no internal offers named as gap); E-08 NYC out; E-09 Austin Series B voluntary out. P2 open role. Finance Sr Analyst (mid GBP82K): E-10 mid GBP76.5K -> band ~6.7% ABOVE the London market -> above-market, Low (single range); E-11 GBP71K Series C partial agrees. No recent internal offers for DevRel or Finance -> named gaps.
criteria: Finance & Accounting is benchmarked in GBP against London GBP evidence only, with no currency conversion, and E-12 (New York, USD) is excluded for geography and currency.

The snapshot's unresolved remote-US anchoring is named as a gap: Remote-US/no-metro points (E-03, E-06) are not treated as full San Francisco comparables, and the response states whether they would change any call.

Staff SRE is read competitive from the SF Series D accepted offer E-01 (~$228K vs $224K midpoint), with the Series C offer E-04 down-weighted and internal accepted offers ($229K/$232K) as corroboration.

Developer Relations uses E-07 as a title-variant match while excluding E-08 (NYC) and E-09 (Austin, Series B), and its verdict carries Low confidence because only one posted range survives and there are no offers.
Finance's band is identified as sitting above the surviving London market (E-10 midpoint GBP76.5K vs GBP82K), at Low confidence, with the absence of internal offers named.

S-006.judge_notes: Tessellate Creative, Series B, Portland OR; window 12 months. Planted note above the table: OR has no pay-transparency mandate, so ALL ranges here are voluntarily posted -> they are aspirational/self-selected and must not carry a verdict on their own where an offer exists; this distinction must be stated once at pool level (not repeated per row). Planted calls: Product Design Sr (mid $138K): E-02 accepted offer $145K -> +5.1% -> LAGGING (just past the line), Medium; E-01 range is voluntary (supporting only); E-03 Seattle (WA mandate) excluded - other metro; internal accepted offers $141K/$143K sit above midpoint but below the external offer - they corroborate pressure without moving the anchor. Content Strategy Mgr (mid $124K): only E-04 (Series A) and E-05 (Series C), both one stage off and pulling opposite ways -> no full comparable -> DEFERRED (averaging them is wrong). Full Stack Sr (mid $163K): E-07 offer $175K -> +7.4% -> LAGGING, Medium-High; E-06 voluntary range agrees; internal accepted $172K and declined $168K corroborate. Full Stack Staff (mid $195K): E-09 offer $198K -> +1.5% -> COMPETITIVE, Medium; E-08 range agrees; no internal offers -> gap. Partnerships Sr Mgr (mid $157K): E-11 (2025-09) out of window; E-12 is a Series A offer (stage partial, cannot anchor); E-10 is a voluntary range only -> no full offer: Deferred is the strict reading; a Low-confidence competitive read from E-10 (+3.8%) is acceptable only if the voluntary-range weakness and the excluded E-11/E-12 are explicit. Internal accepted $160K is context only.
criteria: States that Oregon has no pay-transparency mandate so the ranges are voluntarily posted (aspirational) and weights them below accepted offers.
Content Strategy is Deferred: its only points are one stage off in opposite directions (E-04 Series A, E-05 Series C) and are not averaged into a verdict.
Product Design is read from the accepted offer E-02 ($145K, ~5% above the $138K midpoint) as lagging/at the line, with E-03 (Seattle) excluded and internal offers treated as corroboration.
Partnerships excludes E-11 as out of window (2025-09) and does not let the Series A offer E-12 anchor the verdict; any read from E-10 alone is marked Low or deferred.
Full Stack Senior is read lagging from E-07 (with the internal accepted and declined offers noted) and Full Stack Staff competitive from E-09, each with a confidence tier and reason.

S-007.judge_notes: Auralith Therapeutics, Series B, Boston; window 12 months: points BEFORE October 2025 are out. Boundary: E-13 dated 2025-10 is INSIDE the window; E-10 dated 2025-09 is OUT. MA has no mandate - E-01, E-05, E-06, E-07, E-08, E-09, E-11 are marked 'voluntarily posted' (aspirational, partial); E-13 carries no such note. Planted calls: Computational Biology Sr (mid $157K): E-02 accepted offer $162K -> +3.2% -> competitive at the line (or 'close'/lagging-lean with distance stated); E-01 voluntary range supporting only; E-03 NYC Series C excluded; internal accepted $161K/$164K corroborate; P1. Medium. Clinical Operations AD (mid $185K): E-04 offer $196K -> +5.9% -> LAGGING - the one clear laggard, and it is a P1 open role (hiring risk must be called out); E-05 is Series C and voluntary -> cannot anchor; internal $193K corroborates; Medium. Bioinformatics Staff (mid $171K): E-13 (2025-10, inside window, no voluntary note) is the only full point, mid $174K -> +1.8% -> competitive, LOW (single range); E-06 voluntary (partial) and E-07 Series A + voluntary (dropped); no offers - named gap; P2. Medical Affairs Dir (mid $240K): E-10 offer $248K is OUT (2025-09, stale) and must not be used; E-08 is Series D (two stages above) -> out; E-09 is a voluntary posted range only -> no full comparable -> DEFERRED (a confident verdict from E-09 or the stale E-10 is the wrong call; at most a stated lean). Regulatory Science Sr (mid $153K): E-11 voluntary range and E-12 Series A offer ('Stage partial') are both partial -> DEFERRED, not a verdict. The divergence (one family clearly lags while others sit at market) should be stated rather than a single market line.
criteria: Applies the window boundary precisely: E-13 (2025-10) is kept as in-window and E-10 (2025-09) is excluded as stale, with the cutoff named.
Medical Affairs Director gets no confident verdict: with E-10 stale, E-08 two stages away and E-09 only a voluntarily posted range, it is deferred (or at most a stated lean at Low confidence).
Regulatory Science is deferred or held at Low because its only points are partial (E-11 voluntarily posted, E-12 Series A 'stage partial'), and the Series A offer is not used as the anchor.
Clinical Operations AD is identified as lagging from E-04 ($196K vs $185K, ~6%) and tied to its P1 open-role priority, with E-05 (Series C, voluntary) not anchoring.

Distinguishes voluntarily posted ranges (MA has no mandate) from accepted offers, and reads Computational Biology (E-02 $162K, near the line) and Bioinformatics (E-13 only) with appropriately limited confidence.

S-008.judge_notes: Nexvault Financial, Series C, New York; window 12 months. HEADLINE TRAP: E-03 is a public (post-IPO) company range $260-380K -> excluded on stage; including it in any pool or average is the wrong planted call. Second trap: the declined internal Quant offers cite 'competing offers 15-20% higher' - that is candidate hearsay; turning it into market figures (e.g. '$241K-$254K' or any computed rival offer) cites figures not present in the input -> fails the rubric. One-stage-away points (E-05 Series B 'Senior Legal Counsel (Fintech)', E-06 Series D offer, E-13 Series B, E-14 Series D) are partial and must not anchor or be averaged with full points. Planted calls: Quantitative Research Sr (mid $200K): E-02 accepted offer $232K -> +16% -> LAGGING, clear; E-01 mandated range mid $217.5K agrees (+8.8%); internal accepted $218K and two declines corroborate; P1 critical (trading-desk expansion) -> the hiring risk is the headline. Confidence Medium-High. Compliance Sr Counsel (mid $215K): E-04 mandated range mid $224K -> +4.2% -> lagging lean / at the line, LOW (single range); E-05 and E-06 partial only; no internal offers -> gap. Platform Engineering Sr (mid $185K): E-08 $199K and E-09 $203K offers -> anchor $201K -> +8.6% -> LAGGING, High; E-07 mandated range agrees; internal $194K/$197K corroborate; P1. Product Payments Sr PM (mid $190K): E-11 'Senior PM - Fintech Payments' offer $205K (title variant, in) -> +7.9% -> LAGGING, Medium; E-10 range agrees; internal $198K corroborates; P2. Risk Analytics Mgr (mid $163K): E-12 mandated Series C range mid $171.5K -> +5.2% -> lagging, LOW (single range); E-13/E-14 one stage off -> partial, not averaged; no internal offers -> gap. Market broadly ahead of Nexvault's bands; verdicts must come from the surviving Series C NYC pool.
criteria: E-03 (public, post-IPO range $260K-$380K) is excluded on company stage and does not enter any verdict or average.

Quantitative Research is lagging from E-02 ($232K vs $200K midpoint) and E-01, flagged as a P1 critical hiring risk, with the declined offers' '15-20% higher' claim reported only as candidate-reported context - no figures are derived from it.
One-stage-away points (E-05, E-06, E-13, E-14) are treated as partial/secondary and not used to anchor or averaged with same-stage points.
Platform Engineering is lagging from the two Series C NYC offers (E-08, E-09) with High confidence, and Product Payments is lagging from E-11, accepted as a title-variant match.
Compliance and Risk Analytics each rest on a single same-stage mandated range (E-04, E-12), so their confidence is Low and the absence of internal offer history is named.
